actions\r\nPART A - THE PLAIN-ENGLISH STORY\r\n1. What this system is, in one page\r\nThis is a production-management 
ERP for a leather garment factory. It manages the order-to-production lifecycle and\r\ngives per-piece 
traceability.\r\nIn one sentence: every individual garment carries its own barcode from the moment its breakdown sheet 
is released, and\r\nevery action anyone performs on it - cutting, stitching, storing, inspecting, exporting - is 
scanned and permanently logged\r\nagainst that barcode.\r\nThat single idea is what everything else hangs off.\r\nWhat 
\"per-piece\" actually means\r\nMost factory systems track batches: \"200 jackets went to stitching today.\" This one 
tracks pieces: \"garment PC-004821 - a\r\nsize-50 black CLERMONT, the 17th of its SKU - was cut by Ramesh on the 4th 
from leather lot A-338, stored in drawer\r\nDRW-0042, line-stitched by Farid on the 9th, and is currently waiting for 
final inspection.\"\r\nEvery question a client, a manager or an auditor can ask about one garment has an exact answer, 
months later.\r\nThe five things the system does\r\n┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ 
┌─────────────┐\r\n│ 1. INTAKE │──?│ 2. RELEASE │──?│ 3. PRODUCE │──?│ 4. STORE │──?│ 5. PAY │\r\n└─────────────┘ 
└─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘\r\nClient order DM checks the Every stage is Parts 
merge in Wages computed\r\nsheet uploaded breakdown, then scanned against drawers until from the very\r\nas a 
breakdown. RELEASES it. a piece barcode the garment is same scan\r\nNothing minted Barcodes minted. by the manager 
complete, then events. One\r\nyet - it is a Drawers merged. who owns that released onward line per person\r\ndraft. 
THE MINT. stage. in a batch. per run.\r\nAlongside those five, three supporting systems run continuously: attendance 
(who is on the floor today - production\r\nlogging requires it), materials (what leather and accessories exist and 
what each garment consumed), and dashboards\r\n(what every manager needs to see about their own line).\r\n2. The 
problem it solves\r\nBefore\r\n1. An order sheet arrives. Someone types it into a spreadsheet.\r\n2. Cutting happens. 
Someone writes \"200 cut\" on a whiteboard.\r\n3. A bundle of parts moves to stitching in a plastic crate with a paper 
docket.\r\n4. The docket gets wet, or swapped, or the crate gets split across two tables.\r\n5. A client asks \"which 
hide did the jacket in this complaint come from?\" - nobody knows.\r\n6. Payroll is worked out from tally marks in a 
notebook, two weeks late.\r\n7. A stage runs out of work and nobody notices for a day.\r\nAfter\r\nProblem How the 
system fixes it\r\nBatches lose their identity when split The piece is the tracked unit. There are no bundles. Each 
garment has its own barcode,\r\nso splitting a batch costs nothing\r\nSomeone logs the wrong stage The caller never 
picks a stage. The login screen fixes the cut path; every other stage is\r\ninferred from the piece's own 
history\r\nWork gets logged out of order The sequence gate. A piece cannot be pasted before it is fused\r\nA jacket 
reaches stitching with no lining The merge gate. Line-stitching is blocked until the drawer holds everything 
that\r\ngarment needs\r\nThe wrong worker is credited The skill gate warns when a cutter is logged on a pasting job, 
and every event names\r\nthe worker whose card was scanned\r\nSomeone logs work for a person who is not\r\nin the 
building\r\nProduction logging requires today's attendance\r\nLeather consumption is guesswork The two cut stages 
capture actual consumption per piece, decrementing a named lot\r\nPayroll is a separate re-count Wages are computed 
from the same production events. Nothing is counted twice\r\nA whole batch is lost because one piece 
is\r\nwrong\r\nPartial accept everywhere. One blocked piece never loses the thirty-nine good ones\r\nscanned with 
it\r\nWorkers need logins the factory cannot\r\nmanage\r\nShop-floor workers have no login at all. They have a card. 
An operator scans it\r\nThe design principles behind all of it\r\nSix rules run through every module. They explain 
most of the decisions in this document.\r\n1. The piece is the unit. Not the bundle, not the batch, not the SKU.\r\n2. 
The scanner tells the server who and what - never what stage. Stage is derived. A screen that lets someone pick 
a\r\nstage is a screen that eventually records the wrong one.\r\n3. Partial accept. A batch operation reports per-item 
outcomes and commits the good ones. One bad scan never wastes\r\na manager's whole tray.\r\n4. You retire codes, never 
people or records. A worker leaving retires their card. Their employee row, every production\r\nevent and every wage 
line stay intact for ever.\r\n5. Approval gates are hard, audited state transitions - never a boolean someone can flip 
quietly.\r\n6. When the system is unsure, it asks. Ambiguous material lots, undeclared lining, unconfirmed recipes - 
the system\r\nstops and surfaces the choice rather than guessing.\r\n3. One garment's journey\r\nFollow a single 
jacket - a size-50 black CLERMONT - end to end.\r\nStep 1 - The order arrives\r\nThe client's order becomes a 
ClientOrder with a unique order number, holding Styles (CLERMONT), each holding SKUs\r\n(a colour + size combination 
with a quantity ordered).\r\nClient ── BOGGI MILANO\r\n└── ClientOrder ── BOG-SS27-001\r\n└── Style ── CLERMONT 
(article A-4471, thickness 0.7mm)\r\n└── SKU ── BLACK · 50 · qty 20\r\n└── Piece ── seq 17 of 20  our jacket\r\nStep 
2 - The breakdown sheet is uploaded\r\nThe Direct Manager uploads the breakdown workbook. It is parsed and previewed 
first - nothing is written. When they\r\ncommit, the styles and SKUs land as DRAFT rows.\r\nNothing is minted yet. No 
barcodes, no pieces, no drawers. The DM can now see the whole breakdown as an editable\r\ntable and correct what the 
sheet got wrong - article numbers, thickness, colours, quantities, prices. Breakdown sheets are\r\nhand-made from a 
client order and a spec sheet, and the first pass is routinely wrong in small ways.\r\nStep 3 - Release: the 
mint\r\nWhen the breakdown is correct, the DM releases the styles. For each style they must answer one question that 
cannot be\r\nanswered later:\r\nDoes this garment need a lining?\r\nThis is not optional and it is not inferred. null 
is rejected - \"we never asked\" is a real state and the system will not\r\nproceed from it. The answer is stamped on 
the style, copied onto every piece it mints, and from that moment decides two\r\nthings: whether the garment has a 
lining-cutting stage at all, and whether its drawer must hold both parts before linestitching.\r\nRelease then 
creates, atomically:\r\nthe Piece rows - one per ordered unit, numbered 1..N within the SKU,\r\neach piece's barcode - 
a compact PC-. code that gets printed, plus a long human-readable alias,\r\na Drawer merge - each piece is assigned a 
physical drawer from a finite pool.\r\nOur jacket now exists. It is piece seq 17, barcode PC-004821 , merged to drawer 
DRW-0042 .\r\nThe drawer pool is finite - 200 drawers by default. If a release outruns it, the pieces are still minted 
and still have\r\nbarcodes, but they have no drawer. They cannot be stored, so they cannot pass the merge gate. The 
response says\r\nexactly how many are waiting, and the DM can grow the pool.\r\nStep 4 - Cutting\r\nThe Cutting 
Manager logs in. Their login is their screen - a cutting manager is pinned to the LEATHER_CUT screen and\r\ncannot be 
anywhere else.\r\nAt the table they scan: the worker's card, then the piece barcodes - a tray of thirty at a time. 
They choose the leather\r\nlot (or type article + colour and let the system resolve it) and enter the dcm 
consumed.\r\nThe server:\r\n1. Checks the role may log leather cutting. ?\r\n2. Checks the worker's designation - a 
CUTTER, correct for this stage. ?\r\n3. Checks the sequence - cutting starts a chain, so nothing to check. ?\r\n4. 
Checks the worker is present today. ?\r\n5. Writes one ProductionEvent per piece, links the leather lot, and 
decrements stock once for the whole batch.\r\nThe lining is cut in parallel, by a different manager, on a different 
screen, against the same pieces.\r\nStep 5 - Fusing and pasting\r\nThe Stitching Manager scans the same pieces at the 
next stages. They do not pick a stage - the server infers it. Piece\r\nPC-004821 has completed LEATHER_CUTTING, so the 
next chain stage is FUSING. Scan it again tomorrow and the server\r\ninfers PASTING.\r\nIf someone scans a piece for 
pasting that has not been fused, that one piece comes back sequence_blocked with the\r\nreason. The other twenty-nine 
in the tray still log.\r\nStep 6 - The store\r\nThe cut parts go to the store. The scan order is employee  drawer  
piece, and the drawer comes before the piece\r\ndeliberately: the merge map is the authority, so a piece scanned into 
the wrong drawer is a 409, not a re-assignment.\r\nThe system infers whether the part arriving is leather or lining 
from the piece's own cut history. Once the drawer holds\r\neverything that garment needs - leather, and lining if the 
style declared one - it automatically reaches RECEIVED.\r\nNobody presses a button to assert a fact the server already 
computed.\r\nAccessories are different. Scanning part=ACCESSORY issues the garment's whole accessory kit from the 
style's recipe and\r\nspends stock. It is never inferred - a wrongly guessed kit would move money nobody asked to 
move.\r\nStep 7 - Send\r\nThe Store Manager opens the drawers list, filters to the send queue, ticks the drawers that 
are ready, and sends them as\r\none batch. Sending sets each drawer to SENDED - and that is exactly what the 
production merge gate reads.\r\nOur jacket's drawer is sent. PC-004821 is now eligible for line-stitching.\r\nStep 8 - 
Line stitching onward\r\nThe Stitching Manager scans it. This time the merge gate applies: is the drawer SENDED? Yes. 
The piece logs.\r\nThen SHELL_STITCHING  FINAL_FINISH  FINAL_INSPECTION  PACKAGE_EXPORT. The last two are 
approvals, not\r\nfloor work: no manager role owns them, so only DM/MD/HR can log them.\r\nWhen PACKAGE_EXPORT is 
logged, drawer DRW-0042 recycles back to WAITING and becomes available for the next\r\ngarment.\r\nStep 9 - 
Payroll\r\nAt the end of the fortnight, a piece-rate run is computed for the CLERMONT style. It reads the same 
ProductionEvent\r\nrows that were written on the floor, prices each against the rate in force on the day the work 
happened, and produces\r\none line per employee.\r\nThe run is closed and frozen. It is the document the cash was 
counted against, and from that moment it is never silently\r\nrecomputed.\r\nStep 10 - Forever\r\nSix months later a 
client complaint arrives about one jacket. Scanning its barcode returns: every stage, who worked it, on\r\nwhat date, 
whether it was reworked, which leather lot it was cut from, how much was consumed, which drawer held it, and\r\nwhat 
accessories it was issued.\r\n4. Who does what\r\nRole Value What they do\r\nManaging\r\nDirector\r\nmanaging_director 
Superuser. Bypasses every role gate. Final authority on payroll changes and deletions\r\nDirect Manager direct_manager 
The operational lead. Uploads and releases breakdowns, manages clients and users, sets\r\nrates, runs payroll, grows 
the drawer pool. Also bypasses stage gates\r\nCutting\r\nManager\r\ncutting_manager Logs leather cutting only. Pinned 
to the LEATHER_CUT screen. Creates material lots when\r\nleather arrives\r\nLining Manager lining_manager Logs the 
lining-cut path. Pinned to the LINING_CUT screen\r\nStitching\r\nManager\r\nstitching_manager Logs every post-cut 
floor stage - fusing, pasting, line-stitching, shell-stitching, final\r\nfinish. Also sends drawers\r\nStore Manager 
store_manager Runs the store hub: scans parts into drawers, reads the drawers list, sends batches\r\nonward, records 
off-spec material issues. Store functions only - this role cannot log a\r\nproduction stage\r\nSupervisor supervisor 
Reads the floor roster and dashboards. No attendance writes, no user creation\r\nHR hr Employees, wages visibility, 
designation backfill, attendance operator\r\nSecurity security Gate operator. Scans employee cards in and out. Nothing 
else\r\nMerchandiser merchandiser Client-facing coordinator. Can log in; no route grants them anything yet\r\nClient 
client External login, scoped to their own orders only\r\nViewer viewer Read-only office staff\r\nEmployee employee 
LEGACY - never minted. See below\r\nThe rule that shapes everything: workers get no login\r\nA shop-floor worker has 
no login and no app_user row.\r\nCreating one therefore needs no phone, no email and no password - just a name, a 
designation and a wage type. They\r\nare identified on the floor by their employee barcode, and their attendance is 
entered for them by an operator: Security,\r\nHR, MD or DM.\r\nWhy this matters:\r\nThe factory does not have to 
manage hundreds of passwords for people who do not own smartphones.\r\nThere is no \"worker forgot their password\" 
support burden.\r\nAttendance is done by a gate operator scanning cards, which is faster and more honest than 
self-service.\r\nThe employee role value still exists in the enum only because app_user.role is a native Postgres enum 
and values\r\ncannot be dropped - historical rows may still carry it. Nothing mints it any more.\r\nTwo separations 
worth understanding\r\nThe store manager cannot log production. The person who owns the store is not the person who 
owns the line. Store\r\naccess and stage access are two different questions, and the code keeps them apart 
deliberately.\r\nA cutting manager cannot log a lining cut. Each cut manager is pinned to their own screen by their 
role. The login is\r\nthe screen. That is what makes \"no stage buttons\" possible.\r\n5. What \"done\" looks like at 
each step\r\nStep Done when Where you see it\r\nOrder exists A ClientOrder row with a unique order number GET 
/imports/orders - breakdown_status:\r\nNOT_UPLOADED\r\nBreakdown\r\ncommitted\r\nStyles and SKUs land as DRAFT 
breakdown_status: DRAFT , pieces_minted: 0\r\nBreakdown\r\ncorrected\r\nArticle, thickness, colours, quantities all 
right The breakdown table shows what you expect\r\nRecipe confirmed The style's material spec is signed off 
material_spec_confirmed_at is set\r\nReleased Pieces exist, barcodes minted, drawers merged production_status: 
RELEASED , minted_pieces >\r\n0\r\nDrawers allocated pieces_waiting_for_drawer: 0 The release response, and GET 
/drawers/pool\r\nCut An event at LEATHER_CUTTING (and\r\nLINING_CUTTING if lined)\r\nThe piece's completed 
stages\r\nStored The drawer holds everything the garment needs Drawer state received , can_send: true\r\nSent The 
drawer is SENDED The piece is eligible for line-stitching\r\nFinished An event at PACKAGE_EXPORT The drawer recycles 
to WAITING\r\nPaid A frozen wage run covering the work Run status closed\r\nPART B - THE BUSINESS FLOW IN DETAIL\r\n6. 
Identity and access - who can log in at all\r\nModule: app/modules/users/ · URL prefix: /api/v1/auth and 
/api/v1/users\r\n6.1 One table for every login\r\nA single app_user table authenticates everyone - managers, HR, 
security, clients, viewers. Authorisation is then a matter\r\nof the role column.\r\nWhy one table and not one per 
role: authentication logic lives in exactly one place. Adding a role never means a new\r\nlogin flow or a new table - 
just a new enum value. And every \"who did this\" foreign key points at one column.\r\napp_user\r\n├── phone the LOGIN 
identifier (unique)\r\n├── email optional, also unique\r\n├── password_hash bcrypt\r\n├── role the native PG 
enum\r\n├── is_active\r\n├── must_change_password\r\n├── employee_id  this login IS a person on the payroll\r\n└── 
client_id  this login is an external client, scoped to their orders\r\nThe two optional links are what let one table 
serve very different kinds of user without extra login tables. A manager who\r\nis also on the payroll has employee_id 
set. A client login has client_id set, and every read they perform is scoped to\r\nit.\r\n6.2 The two 
gates\r\nrequire_roles(...) - the per-route gate. MD and DM are superusers and bypass every one of them.\r\nA note on 
that bypass: the spec target is for MD alone to be the superuser and DM to be operational-only. DM still\r\nbypasses 
during the MD rollout so the existing seeded god-account does not lose access. Drop DM from that set\r\nonce an MD 
owner is confirmed in every environment.\r\nblock_employees - a deny-list dependency applied at the router level in 
main.py , so a new route is closed to the\r\nlegacy employee role unless someone opens it deliberately. Most read 
routes use bare get_current_user ; retrofitting\r\nan allow-list to every one of them is not realistic, and any route 
missed is a leak.\r\nThree router groups stay unlocked: auth, users, and attendance - plus /barcode/resolve , which 
must stay reachable\r\nfrom the attendance screen so a gate operator can resolve a card.\r\n6.3 Who may create 
whom\r\nPOST /users admits DM, HR and MD at the door - but which role may be granted is decided in the service 
against\r\nthe caller's own authority.\r\nPOST /users/clients provisions a client login bound to a client_id . DM and 
MD only - HR is deliberately\r\nexcluded. Binding a login to a client grants cross-tenant read access to that client's 
orders; that is a commercial\r\ndecision, not an employee-admin one.\r\n7. People - employees, cards, and the no-login 
rule\r\nModule: app/modules/employees/ · URL prefix: /api/v1/employees\r\n7.1 Creating a worker\r\nThe common case is 
deliberately tiny:\r\n{ \"name\": \"Ramesh Kumar\", \"designation\": \"CUTTER\", \"wage_type\": \"piece_rate\" }\r\nNo 
phone, no email, no password, no role. What comes back includes an employee barcode - minted in the 
same\r\ntransaction so the card can be printed immediately.\r\n7.2 Creating staff\r\nPassing an explicit staff role 
mints a login alongside the employee row. That path does need a phone and a password.\r\nPermitted here: HR, 
Supervisor, Cutting/Lining/Stitching Manager, Security, Merchandiser. Excluded: DM and MD\r\n(created via 
user-creation) and employee (workers get no login at all).\r\nA rule that used to be wrong: a MONTHLY wage type used 
to auto-mint an employee login. It no longer does.\r\nWage type is a payroll fact and says nothing about system 
access.\r\n7.3 Designations - a controlled vocabulary\r\nDesignations are always uppercase, normalised on write: \" 
shell tailor \" and \"Shell-Tailor\" both become\r\nSHELL_TAILOR .\r\nWhy it is controlled and not free text: the 
moment it is free text, Cutter , cutter and CUTTTER become three\r\ndifferent skills and the skill gate is 
decorative.\r\nUnknown designations are kept, not rejected - seeded data carries job titles nobody has catalogued, and 
failing\r\nemployee creation on an unrecognised title would block HR. The skill gate treats an uncatalogued 
designation as\r\nunknown and passes it (fail-open), tightening as HR backfills the vocabulary.\r\n7.4 Names are 
unique\r\nA collision is prefixed IN-CHAL . Two people called Ramesh Kumar are two rows, and the floor can tell them 
apart.\r\n7.5 Leaving\r\nDeleting an employee is a soft delete: is_active: false , and their barcode is retired. DM/MD 
only - HR can edit but\r\nnot remove.\r\nThe employee row, every production event and every wage line stay intact. You 
delete the scannable code, never the\r\nperson or their record. Scanning the retired card returns 410 Gone - 
distinguishable from \"never existed\", so the screen\r\ncan say \"this card was deactivated\" rather than \"invalid 
barcode\".\r\n7.6 Salary is redacted\r\nThe roster returns salary only to HR, DM and MD. And the roster itself is 
internal - a CLIENT or VIEWER token is refused\r\noutright, because the row carries phone and email too.\r\n8. 
Clients, orders, styles and SKUs\r\nModule: app/modules/clients/ · URL prefix: /api/v1/clients\r\n8.1 The 
hierarchy\r\nClient name, country, code (KJ, GGZ.), currency, size system\r\n└── ClientOrder order_number (unique), 
dates, sea cut-off, ship mode\r\n└── Style name, article, thickness, code (unique), season, refs, price\r\n└── SKU 
colour + size + qty_ordered; code unique per style\r\n└── Piece ONE physical garment; seq 1..N within the SKU\r\nPiece 
is the tracked unit. Its code is the parent barcode.\r\n8.2 Two dates that matter commercially\r\ndelivery_deadline - 
when the client expects it.\r\nsea_cutoff_date - the last day to make sea freight.\r\nMissing the sea cut-off means 
air freight, which is the single biggest margin event in the business. That is why it is an\r\nalert on every manager 
dashboard, not a report line.\r\n8.3 Style-level production state\r\nEach style carries its own release 
lifecycle:\r\nField Meaning\r\nproduction_status DRAFT  RELEASED  CANCELLED\r\nreleased_at / released_by Who minted 
the pieces, and when\r\nneeds_lining The DM's declaration. Nullable - null means 
unanswered\r\nmaterial_spec_confirmed_at / _by The recipe sign-off\r\nmaterial_spec_no_accessories The explicit \"this 
garment takes none\"\r\n8.4 Tenancy\r\nA CLIENT login is pinned to its own client_id on every client-facing read - the 
client list, the styles list, orders,\r\nanalytics, production reads. A cross-tenant id resolves to 404 rather than 
403, because existence itself is information.\r\n8.5 Delete vs deactivate\r\nDELETE /clients/{id} works only on a 
client with no orders - a mistyped or duplicate row. A client with orders is a\r\n409, because the cascade would take 
their orders, styles, SKUs, and every piece, production event and wage line hanging\r\noff them. The error names the 
exact call to make instead: PATCH with {\"is_active\": false} .\r\n9. Import and the release gate - where garments are 
born\r\nModule: app/modules/imports/ · URL prefix: /api/v1/imports\r\nThis module is where a spreadsheet becomes real 
garments. It is the highest-consequence surface in Phase 1, and it is\r\ndeliberately a two-phase commit.\r\n9.1 
Preview, then commit\r\nPOST /imports/preview ── parse the workbook, return a summary + warnings. WRITES 
NOTHING.\r\nPOST /imports/commit ── parse again, then write SKUs into the named order. Idempotent.\r\nThe order number 
is validated first - the endpoint 404s rather than create an order, so a typo cannot silently spawn a\r\nphantom 
order.\r\nThe upload itself is guarded three ways: extension, a hard size cap streamed rather than read into memory, 
and a zipcontainer check (an .xlsx is a zip; anything renamed to .xlsx that is not a valid zip is rejected before it 
reaches the\r\nparser).\r\n9.2 Commit mints nothing\r\nThis is the change that matters most.\r\nPOST /imports/commit 
writes DRAFT styles and SKUs. It creates no pieces, no barcodes and no drawer\r\nmerges. The response says so 
explicitly: release_required: true , pieces_minted: 0 .\r\nThe sheet lands as an editable table. The DM reviews it and 
corrects what is wrong.\r\n9.3 The breakdown table\r\nGET /imports/breakdown/{order_number} is the screen between 
upload and production: styles with their SKUs, each\r\nrow carrying its production_status .\r\nDRAFT rows are editable 
and have minted nothing.\r\nRELEASED rows have real barcoded garments behind them and are read-only.\r\nCorrections 
are made through three doors:\r\nPATCH /breakdown/skus/{id} - the table row. Can edit the SKU and its parent style in 
one call, in one\r\ntransaction, so the screen can never end up with the colour saved and the article not.\r\nPATCH 
/breakdown/styles/{id} - the style header, which has no SKU to hang off.\r\nDELETE /breakdown/skus/{id} - drop a line 
the sheet should not have had. DRAFT with zero minted pieces only.\r\nAll of them 409 once the style is RELEASED: its 
pieces carry printed barcodes, and rewriting the breakdown behind a\r\ngarment already on the floor is how a factory 
loses traceability.\r\n9.4 The release - the mint\r\nPOST /imports/breakdown/{order_number}/release is the moment 
garments come into existence. Atomically, and only\r\nnow:\r\n1. Piece rows - one per ordered unit.\r\n2. Per-piece 
barcodes - the compact PC-XXXXXX that gets printed, plus the long alias so older labels still resolve.\r\n3. The 
drawer merge - each piece assigned a drawer from the pool.\r\n4. The style stamped RELEASED with the actor and time, 
plus an audit_log row.\r\n9.5 The lining declaration\r\nEvery style must declare whether it needs a lining. Three 
shapes are accepted:\r\nShape Meaning\r\n{\"styles\": [{\"style_id\": ., \"needs_lining\":\r\ntrue}, .]}\r\nThe 
contract. Each style carries its own answer\r\n{\"style_ids\": [...], \"needs_lining\": true} Broadcast. One human 
answer covering the whole list - still a\r\ndeclaration\r\n{\"style_ids\": [...]} alone Deprecated. Falls back to 
inferring the lining requirement from the\r\nstyle name\r\nA per-style answer overrides the broadcast, so the common 
case can be sent once and the exceptions named.\r\nThree things make this worth the friction:\r\nnull is rejected. 
\"We never asked\" is a real and different state from \"no\", and release will not proceed from it.\r\nThe declaration 
outranks the system's own guess, in both directions - including declaring a style named \".KNIT\"\r\nas leather-only. 
That is the point of asking: inference off a style name cannot know that a particular wool shell has no\r\nlining, and 
the DM holding the spec sheet can.\r\nIt cannot be changed after release. Pieces are minted against it and their 
barcodes are printed.\r\nThe request body uses extra=\"forbid\" , so a misspelt or misplaced field is a 422 naming it 
- rather than a silent no-op\r\non the one field this endpoint exists to capture.\r\n9.6 Partial accept\r\nAn 
already-released style comes back in rejected with its reason; the rest still release. Read minted , not the 
HTTP\r\nstatus.\r\n9.7 The drawer-pool warning\r\nWatch minted.pieces_waiting_for_drawer . The pool is finite. Pieces 
beyond the free drawers are minted with barcodes\r\nbut nowhere to be stored - so they cannot pass the merge gate 
until a drawer frees up or the pool is grown.\r\ngrow_drawer_pool: true on the release call, or POST /drawers/pool 
afterwards, clears it.\r\n9.8 The order index\r\nGET /imports/orders is the index every breakdown screen opens from, 
with a rolled-up status per order:\r\nbreakdown_status Meaning\r\nNOT_UPLOADED The order exists; no breakdown 
committed yet\r\nDRAFT Sheet uploaded, nothing released, nothing minted\r\nPARTIALLY_RELEASED Some styles in 
production, some still editable\r\nRELEASED Every live style released and minting pieces\r\nCANCELLED Every style on 
the order was cancelled\r\nOrdered most-recently-worked-on first - the newest of the order's creation and its 
last-written style. The client's\r\norder_date says nothing about what the factory is handling now.\r\n10. The barcode 
system - the spine\r\nModule: app/modules/barcode/ · URL prefix: /api/v1/barcode\r\n10.1 One registry, one front 
door\r\nbarcode_registry is the single table every scan resolves through. Each printed code - a piece, a material lot, 
a drawer,\r\nan employee card - has exactly one row carrying its type , its status , and a nullable foreign key to the 
domain row it\r\nnames.\r\nGET /barcode/resolve?code=. is one indexed lookup:\r\nOutcome Meaning\r\n404 Unknown 
code\r\n410 Gone Retired code - \"this was deactivated; the record and history are intact\"\r\n200 The code's type 
plus a live payload for that type\r\nThat 404/410 split is the whole point. A retired employee card and a typo are 
different facts, and the screen should say\r\ndifferent things.\r\nRetirement applies to every barcode type, not just 
employee cards. A retired lot label and a deactivated piece\r\nmust not silently resolve either.\r\n10.2 The 
types\r\nType Minted when Editable?\r\nPIECE Release No - permanent garment identity\r\nLEATHER_LOT / LINING_LOT / 
ACCESSORY_LOT Material lot created No\r\nDRAWER Pool creation No - static code, recycling state\r\nEMPLOYEE Employee 
created Yes - reissue / deactivate\r\n10.3 One piece, two codes\r\nSince the compact code arrived, a piece has two 
active registry rows:\r\nthe small PC-004821 that is printed and scanned - the primary,\r\nits old long 
KJ2451-CLERMONT-57-M-017 code, kept alive so labels printed before the change still resolve - flagged\r\nis_alias: 
true .\r\nis_alias is a stored flag, not inferred from the prefix. Every per-order count and the whole history list 
select\r\ntype=PIECE rows; with two rows per piece and no discriminator, minted doubles, balance goes negative, 
the\r\nduplicates integrity proof reads as broken, and the history table shows each garment twice. Those queries need 
to name\r\nthe rule they mean - \"the code happens to start with PC-\" is not that rule.\r\nA resolve on a legacy code 
still works and returns is_alias: true , so the screen can nudge the operator to reprint the\r\nlabel.\r\n10.4 The 
employee card lifecycle - history is sacred\r\nReissue (lost or damaged card): retire the old code, mint a new one. 
History untouched.\r\nDeactivate (worker leaves): flip the registry status to RETIRED  resolve returns 410. The 
employee row, all production\r\nevents, and all wage lines stay intact.\r\nBoth are audited. PATCH 
/employees/{id}/barcode is where they live - mounted under /employees because that is\r\nwhere the frontend expects 
it, but owned by the barcode module because employee barcodes are a barcode concern.\r\n10.5 Resolve answers the next 
question too\r\nA scan does not just say what the code is. It also carries:\r\nField Meaning\r\nnext_expected_scan 
\"PIECE\" / \"DRAWER\" / null - which code to present next. Answered for every type, including\r\nEMPLOYEE, which is 
the first scan of every workflow\r\nnext_stage +\r\nnext_stage_label\r\nThe production stage this piece is due at, 
derived by the same helper the write path uses\r\nnext_stage_blocked_reason Set when that stage cannot be logged yet - 
e.g. the drawer has not been sent\r\nThat last pair matters: the stage is still reported even when blocked. The screen 
shows where the piece is going and what\r\nis holding it there.\r\nWhy one shared helper: next_chain_stage() is pure 
and takes a set of completed operation codes. Both the write\r\npath (which decides what a scan logs) and the read 
paths (which tell the screen what is coming) call it. Two copies of\r\nthat loop would drift, and the drift is 
invisible until a screen offers a stage the log then refuses.\r\n10.6 Printing\r\nPOST /barcode/print returns a 
Code128-ready payload for a set of codes, or for every piece of a SKU or order. Each\r\nlabel carries the code to 
encode plus a label_line - the order number, article, style, colour, size and serial, pre-joined\r\nand ready to 
typeset underneath.\r\nThere is also a material barcode screen ( GET /barcode/materials ), which exists because lots 
minted a code at creation\r\nand nobody could reprint it once the first label was lost.\r\n10.7 The order-level 
integrity proof\r\nGET /barcode/orders/{id}/analytics reports planned vs generated vs balance, per order and per 
style, plus:\r\nduplicates - should always be 0. It is the proof that minting stayed idempotent.\r\nhalf_minted - some 
pieces exist but not all.\r\nfully_generated - the order is complete.\r\n11. Materials, lots and the style 
recipe\r\nModule: app/modules/materials/ · URL prefixes: /api/v1/materials , /api/v1/suppliers , /api/v1/styles\r\nTwo 
related things live here: what the factory HAS (lots), and what a garment NEEDS (the recipe). They meet at 
six\r\nidentity columns and nowhere else.\r\n11.1 Three categories, strict fields\r\nEvery lot must carry exactly its 
category's fields, or the API rejects it with a 422. Creating a lot mints a child barcode -\r\nthat is how material 
formally enters inventory.\r\nCategory / subtype Required attributes Quantity field UOM Filters\r\nLeather thickness, 
dcm dcm dcm article, colour, thickness\r\nLining / plain thickness, mtrs mtrs mtrs article, colour, 
thickness\r\nLining / ribs kg kg kg article, colour\r\nLining / knit pcs pcs pcs article, colour\r\nAccessory / button 
size, count count pcs article, colour, size\r\nAccessory / zip size, count count pcs article, colour, 
size\r\nAccessory / thread thickness, mtrs mtrs mtrs article, colour, thickness\r\nAccessory / other description, 
count count pcs article, colour\r\narticle and colour are required for every material. GET 
/materials/spec?category=&subtype= returns this list at\r\nruntime, so the frontend renders the right form and the 
right filter boxes without hard-coding anything.\r\nA (category, subtype) pair not in that table is rejected - the 
system does not invent a shape for a material class it\r\nwas not told about.\r\n11.2 Three stored numbers\r\non_hand 
a real column - physically in the building\r\nreserved a reservation ledger - committed to a required 
quantity\r\navailable on_hand - reserved  DERIVED, never stored\r\navailable is never stored, so the two can never 
drift.\r\nCategory-specific attributes live in a JSON column rather than twenty mostly-null columns. The four the 
queries actually\r\nfilter on - article, colour, thickness, size - are promoted to real indexed columns.\r\n11.3 The 
lot picker\r\nGET /materials/lots is the endpoint the cut screen uses to turn \"black sheep glass, 0.7mm\" into a lot 
id.\r\nThree material GETs, three different jobs - worth keeping straight:\r\nEndpoint Returns\r\n/materials/spec The 
form definition - which boxes to render\r\n/materials/lots The rows, with lot ids\r\n/materials/stock Aggregate 
totals, with the lot ids summed away\r\nThe picker also does two helpful things: last_used_for_sku pre-selects the lot 
this SKU was last cut from (and shows\r\nthat it did), and passing required makes each lot report covers_required - so 
a lot that cannot cover the batch is\r\ngreyed out before the cut instead of warning after it.\r\nExhausted lots are 
returned, not hidden. A manager searching for a lot they know exists must find it, with\r\navailable: 0 explaining 
itself.\r\n11.4 Editing a lot - three different operations\r\nThe stock screen deliberately splits what looks like one 
action into three:\r\nOperation What it changes Why separate\r\nPATCH /lots/{id} Identity - article, 
colour,\r\nthickness, size, supplier\r\nPATCH\r\n/lots/{id}/adjust\r\nQuantity, as a delta with a\r\nmandatory reason, 
audited\r\nIt records a movement, so the ledger still adds up and someone\r\ncan ask a year later why 40 dcm 
disappeared\r\nDELETE /lots/{id} Retires the lot and its barcode Never a hard delete - cut events point at this lot 
and are the\r\nconsumption history the costing screens are built on\r\nCategory, subtype, UOM and on_hand are not 
patchable. Moving LEATHERLINING would leave a lot measured in\r\ndcm claiming to be metres, and every cut event 
already pointing at it would silently re-denominate. Setting on_hand\r\ndirectly would make the stock and the movement 
history disagree with no record of who changed it.\r\nRetiring is presented as \"retire\", not \"delete\". A scan of 
the old label returns 410 Gone (\"this lot was retired\"), not 404\r\n(\"invalid barcode\").\r\n11.5 Receiving\r\nPOST 
/materials/receive records approved and rejected quantities separately.\r\nApproved quantity is added to 
stock.\r\nRejected quantity is logged - supplier quality history.\r\nA PO mismatch is a 409 unless a DM/MD sends 
approve_mismatch: true , which receives it into a new substitute\r\nlot rather than quietly re-labelling the old 
one.\r\n11.6 Supplier orders\r\nA simple two-state manual flow: ORDERED  ARRIVED. Raising an order validates the 
requested article against the\r\nchosen or suggested supplier's catalogue. GET /materials/stock suggests a supplier 
when short.\r\n11.7 The style material spec - the recipe\r\nMounted at /api/v1/styles/{style_id}/material-spec . This 
is what one garment of a style needs: its leather, its\r\nlining, and every accessory.\r\nStyleMaterialSpec (one row 
per line)\r\n├── style_id\r\n├── sku_id null = the style-wide default; set = a per-SKU override\r\n├── category / 
subtype / article / colour / thickness / size\r\n├── qty_per_piece\r\n├── uom DERIVED from (category, subtype) - never 
taken from the client\r\n└── material_lot_id optional explicit binding\r\nThe UOM is derived, not accepted. Buttons 
are pcs, thread is mtrs - the unit is a property of the material kind. uom\r\nstays in the request contract only so a 
client can round-trip a GET without stripping fields.\r\n11.8 Confirming the recipe unlocks release\r\nPOST 
/styles/{id}/material-spec/confirm is the sign-off, and it is a separate call from release on purpose: the DM\r\ncan 
finish the recipe days earlier, and the release screen can render release_blockers before the button is 
pressed\r\nrather than explaining a rejection afterwards.\r\nno_accessories: true is the DM stating \"this garment 
takes none\". It is the only thing that lets a style with an empty\r\naccessory list through the release gate - an 
empty list on its own is ambiguous (nobody entered them yet?), and\r\nreleasing that silently is how a whole order 
reaches the store with no kit. Sending true while accessory lines exist is a\r\n422, not a precedence rule.\r\n11.9 
The requirement screen\r\nGET /styles/{id}/material-spec/requirement is qty_ordered × per-piece against what is on the 
shelf, per line.\r\nThis is the screen that should stop an order, and the moment to read it is before release. 
Afterwards the garments\r\nexist and a shortfall is a stoppage rather than a purchase order. short_by and 
suggested_supplier feed straight into\r\nPOST /suppliers/orders .\r\n11.10 The frozen recipe and its escape 
hatch\r\nOnce a style is RELEASED, its recipe cannot be edited - its garments are already being issued against 
it.\r\nA wrong article is corrected by recording what was actually handed over: POST /materials/issues records a 
material\r\nissued to one garment outside its spec, and spends stock.\r\nIt is repeatable on purpose: three 
corrections on one garment are three real events, and none of them makes the kit\r\nchecklist think a spec line was 
satisfied.\r\nThe store manager can call it - waiting for a DM to record a swapped button is how the correction stops 
being made at\r\nall.\r\n12. Production - one log, two doors, four gates\r\nModule: app/modules/production/ · URL 
prefix: /api/v1/production\r\n12.1 The pipeline\r\nLEATHER_CUTTING ┐\r\n├─ parallel cut paths, per 
piece\r\nLINING_CUTTING ┘\r\n FUSING  PASTING  [ MERGE GATE ]  LINE_STITCHING  SHELL_STITCHING\r\n FINAL_FINISH 
 FINAL_INSPECTION  PACKAGE_EXPORT\r\nTwo entry stages, one join. Leather and lining are cut independently, by 
different managers, on different screens. They\r\nhave no predecessor. Everything after the drawer merge is a single 
linear chain.\r\nThat breaks the naive \"one linear predecessor\" model, so the code is explicit about it: 
predecessor() returns the\r\nleather-side predecessor for the leather chain, and None for LINE_STITCHING - because 
line-stitching's precondition is\r\nnot \"pasting done\" but \"leather and lining both merged in the drawer\", which 
the completeness gate enforces, not the\r\nsequence gate.\r\nWhy stage order is in code, not config. The operation 
table stays the source of truth for labels and rates. But the\r\nstage order, the two parallel cut paths, the role  
stage map and the designation  stage map are business law.\r\nEncoding order against Operation.sequence alone would 
mean a stray UPDATE to a sequence number silently\r\nreorders the factory. Codes are stable; sequence numbers are 
not.\r\n12.2 One endpoint, two doors, no stage buttons\r\nPOST /production/log is the whole floor's logging surface. 
The caller sends an actor (an employee, by barcode or id)\r\nand targets (pieces, by barcode or sku + seqs).\r\nThe 
caller never sends a stage.\r\nA cut screen (LEATHER_CUT / LINING_CUT) fixes the cut stage.\r\nOtherwise the stage is 
inferred from each piece's own history - the next chain stage after the furthest one it 
has\r\ncompleted.\r\n\"Furthest completed, plus one\" rather than \"first not completed\": a piece that was reworked 
or logged out of order\r\nshould advance from how far it has actually got, not stall at the earliest gap.\r\nThe 
screen context is derived from the role. A cutting manager is pinned to LEATHER_CUT; a lining manager 
to\r\nLINING_CUT; a stitching manager or supervisor to PIPELINE. Any value they send is ignored. Only DM/MD/HR - 
who\r\nlegitimately log any stage - may pass an explicit override.\r\nBoth doors POST the same shape. The router 
resolves barcodes to ids; the service sees ids only.\r\n12.3 The four gates\r\nCheapest and most-likely-to-fail 
first.\r\n# Gate Scope On failure\r\n1 ROLE - may this role log this stage? Whole request 403\r\n2 SKILL - may this 
designation work this stage? Per piece Warning, still logged\r\n3 SEQUENCE - has the piece completed the previous 
chain stage? Per piece sequence_blocked\r\n4 MERGE - for LINE_STITCHING only: is the drawer SENDED? Per piece 
merge_blocked\r\nGate 1 is whole-request because the role is wrong for the whole batch - there is nothing per-piece 
about it. Gates 2-4\r\nare per-piece so that one bad piece never loses the thirty-nine good ones a manager scanned 
with it.\r\nMD and DM bypass the role gate. HR does too.\r\nGate 2 is a warning, not a block. A cutter logged on a 
pasting job still records the work; the anomaly comes back in\r\nskill_warnings with the employee, their designation, 
the stage and a note. Blocking it would mean a helper covering a\r\nshift cannot be recorded at all.\r\nRework is 
permissive and bypasses gates 3 and 4. A piece returning to a stage it already passed is legitimate -\r\nflagged, 
never blocked.\r\n12.4 The door gate\r\nPOST /production/log also carries a role dependency at the door, in front of 
the per-stage gate.\r\nThe route deliberately had none for a while, on the reasoning that the role gate is 
stage-specific. That is true for a piece\r\nwith a resolvable stage - and it left a gap for one without. A piece that 
has not been cut yet resolves to no stage on the\r\nPIPELINE screen, so Gate 1 never runs and the request comes back 
201 with everything in the not_cut bucket, for any\r\nauthenticated token.\r\nNothing was ever written on that path, 
so it was not a data leak. It was worse as an answer: a store login was told\r\n\"nothing logged, cut it first\", 
implying it may log once the piece is cut - when in fact its scan will 403 the moment a stage\r\nresolves. The role 
that cannot log anything is now told so at the door, once.\r\nSTORE_MANAGER is deliberately absent from the logger 
set.\r\n12.5 Consumption\r\nThe two cut stages only capture material consumption per piece and decrement stock once 
per batch, in the same\r\ntransaction as the events.\r\nThe lot link lives on the event - the act of cutting - never 
on the piece.\r\nThree doors supply the lot:\r\n1. Lot id - the screen already picked one.\r\n2. Article + colour + 
optional thickness - the cutting manager types what is on the hide, and the router resolves it\r\nthrough the same lot 
picker the UI uses.\r\n3. use_style_spec: true - take the dcm from the style's recipe.\r\nTwo of those refuse to 
guess:\r\nNo lot matches  404 naming the spec and telling you to add the delivery first.\r\nSeveral lots match  409 
naming up to five candidates with their availability. Silently taking the first would\r\ndecrement stock from a lot 
the manager never chose - a wrong number in the one ledger the factory reconciles\r\nagainst, and invisible.\r\nA 
batch whose pieces disagree on the spec dcm  422 naming both values. Pieces from two SKUs with different\r\noverrides 
have no single number, and picking one would write the wrong consumption against half the garments.\r\nuse_style_spec 
is off by default, deliberately: omitting both dcm and the flag still returns today's 422, so no existing\r\nclient 
silently changes behaviour on the one branch that guards the leather ledger. The recipe is normally reached 
the\r\nother way round - /production/piece-state returns suggested_dcm_per_piece and the screen prefills the field, 
so\r\nthe operator still confirms the number that reaches the ledger.\r\nA cut that consumes more than the lot has 
available is still recorded. Stock drifts and the garment is physically cut;\r\nthe shortfall comes back in 
stock_warning rather than silently driving on_hand negative.\r\n12.6 The scan-time read\r\nGET /production/piece-state 
is what a barcode scan should return: one piece, not a SKU.\r\nSend code + employee_barcode and read three 
fields:\r\nField Meaning\r\ncurrent_stage Where the piece is now\r\nnext_stage What this scan would log - never chosen 
by hand\r\nready_to_log true  POST the log immediately. false  show blockers . null  no employee was sent, so 
the\r\nquestion is unanswered - which is not the same as blocked, and must not be rendered as one\r\nIt exists because 
stage inference and all three per-piece gates used to run only at write time, so the UI had to guess: it\r\nmade the 
operator pick a stage by hand, and it left later stage cards scannable before their predecessor was done. 
This\r\nanswers both from the server, using the very same predicates the log enforces - so a card the UI opens is a 
card the\r\nlog will accept.\r\nIt also carries the piece's drawer , its stages[] cards (each completed / next / 
locked / not_applicable , with the\r\ngate and reason for a locked one), the actor block (name, designation, whether 
they are checked in, any skill anomaly),\r\nthe material_requirement kit checklist, and sku progress.\r\n12.7 The 
response\r\nPOST /production/log returns a rich per-piece result, because a batch of forty is forty separate 
outcomes:\r\nField Meaning\r\nstage The stage logged. \"MIXED\" when a PIPELINE batch spanned several; null 
only\r\nwhen nothing resolved\r\nstage_by_piece The truth for a mixed batch\r\nlogged / rework / not_found 
/\r\ncompleted\r\nThe classic buckets\r\nsequence_blocked / skill_blocked /\r\nmerge_blocked / 
role_blocked\r\nPer-piece refusals\r\nblocked[] Every rejection with its cause - {piece, stage, gate, 
reason}\r\nskill_warnings[] Gate-2 anomalies that still logged\r\nstock_warning A cut that went short\r\nsku_progress 
{total, done, remaining, closed} for the stage just logged. closed: true\r\nmeans stop offering this style for 
scanning\r\ndrawer_by_piece Each piece's drawer state\r\nkit_by_piece Deliberately lean - kit_required , kit_status , 
outstanding . A forty-piece\r\nbatch carrying full requirement blocks would dwarf the rest of the response\r\nmessage 
One sentence for the scan screen\r\npreview: true runs the whole thing as a dry run: computes every bucket, writes 
nothing.\r\n12.8 The retired routes\r\nPOST /production/cutting and POST /production/scan return 410 Gone with a 
message pointing at /log . A\r\ndeleted route 404s, and a 404 on a screen that worked yesterday reads as \"the server 
is broken\". 410 says the removal was\r\ndeliberate.\r\n13. Drawers and the merge gate\r\nModule: app/modules/drawers/ 
· URL prefix: /api/v1/drawers\r\n13.1 A static code with a recycling state\r\nWAITING ──(release)──? MERGED ──? 
HOLDING_LEATHER ─┐\r\n│ HOLDING_LINING ──┼──? HOLDING_BOTH\r\n│ │\r\n└────────────────────────┴──? RECEIVED ──? 
SENDED\r\n│\r\n(piece ships) ───────────┘\r\n\r\nWAITING\r\nThe code never changes. The state cycles. 
current_piece_id moves over the drawer's life.\r\n13.2 The store scan\r\nThe order is employee  drawer  piece, and 
all three are enforced server-side.\r\nThe employee scan is mandatory. The store scan used to accept no actor at all - 
the one door on the floor where\r\n\"who did this\" was unanswerable. A rule the frontend alone enforces is a rule 
that disappears the moment anything\r\nelse calls the API.\r\nThe drawer comes before the piece because the merge map 
is the authority. A piece scanned into the wrong drawer\r\nis a 409, not a re-assignment.\r\npart is optional. The 
server infers LEATHER vs LINING from the piece's own cut history and what the drawer is still\r\nmissing. Send it only 
to override.\r\npart=ACCESSORY is explicit-only and never inferred. The worst a wrong LEATHER/LINING guess can do is 
set the wrong\r\nboolean, which a human can undo. An inferred ACCESSORY would spend stock - it decrements every 
accessory lot on\r\nthe style's spec - so a mis-inference would move money nothing on the floor asked to move.\r\nThe 
accessory scan is idempotent: a second tap issues nothing and returns the same 200.\r\nEvery scan returns the kit 
block, cut parts included, so the person at the drawer can see what accessories the garment\r\nstill needs without 
leaving the screen.\r\n13.3 Completeness, not sequence\r\nThe gate is about completeness, not order:\r\nA lined jacket 
needs leather and lining before its drawer is complete.\r\nA leather-only piece ( needs_lining: false ) is complete on 
leather alone.\r\nRECEIVED is now reached automatically the moment a drawer holds everything its garment needs. The 
old flow -\r\npress RECEIVED, then press SEND, one drawer at a time - is gone, because RECEIVED asserted a fact the 
server had\r\nalready computed.\r\nneeds_lining on every drawer row is the EFFECTIVE requirement, resolved from the 
style, the SKU and the cut\r\nhistory - not the stored piece.needs_lining flag, which is written once at release and 
is wrong for most of a live\r\norder. When the two disagree, lining_reason says why.\r\n13.4 Send - the decision that 
stayed\r\nSEND is a decision, so it stayed. And it became plural, because the store never releases one drawer at a 
time.\r\nPOST /drawers/send takes drawer ids and nothing else. There is no destination to pick: lining is upstream of 
the store,\r\nso a merged drawer has exactly one way forward.\r\nSending sets each drawer to SENDED, which is exactly 
what the production merge gate reads. The whole selected bunch\r\nof pieces becomes eligible for LINE_STITCHING in one 
action.\r\nPartial accept: a drawer that is not yet RECEIVED comes back in not_ready with its reason; the rest are 
still sent. Check\r\ncount_sent , not the HTTP status.\r\nWho may send: MD, DM, Store Manager - and the Stitching 
Manager. That last one is a deliberate scope change:\r\nsending is what releases a batch into line-stitching, and on 
the floor the stitching manager is the one who walks to the\r\nstore and takes the drawers. Requiring a DM to press 
the button made the store a bottleneck on a decision the stitching\r\nmanager was already making physically. It is a 
role grant on the store surface, not a production permission -\r\nSTAGE_ROLE_ACCESS is untouched. Cutting and lining 
managers are still excluded: they put parts in; they do not decide\r\nwhat leaves.\r\n13.5 The drawers list\r\nGET 
/drawers is the store's working screen.\r\nOrdered most-recently-worked-on first by default. \"Worked on\" means the 
newest of: merged to a garment, part\r\nscanned in, received, sent, or released back to the pool. Every row carries 
last_activity_at and last_activity\r\n( \"merged\" / \"scanned\" / \"received\" / \"sent\" / \"released\" ) - a 
timestamp with no verb tells the operator when\r\nsomething happened but not what, which is the half they need to 
decide whether to open the drawer.\r\nThis replaced an ordering that could not see three of those five events: a merge 
and a store scan wrote no timestamp at\r\nall, and a release nulled the received/sent stamps, so the drawer that had 
just shipped sank to the bottom.\r\nPass sort=seq for the print sheet - DRW-0001.DRW-0200 in drawer order.\r\nTwo 
search affordances work together: code= is a case-insensitive contains, so \"42\" and \"drw-004\" both 
work.\r\npin_codes= replays the client's own recently-searched list to float those drawers above everything else - 
nothing about\r\na search is stored server-side, because that is one operator's session, not a fact about the factory. 
Pinned rows are flagged\r\nso the UI can band them separately.\r\nsendable=true is the send queue - drawers that hold 
everything their garment needs, waiting for someone to tick and\r\nsend them. can_send applies the same rule the send 
endpoint enforces, so the queue can never offer a row the server\r\nrefuses.\r\nA row with barcode: null is a drawer 
with no registry code. It cannot be scanned, so print nothing for it - and the list\r\nshows it rather than silently 
dropping it, because that is a broken label somebody needs to fix.\r\n13.6 The pool\r\nThe pool is fixed at 200 and 
grows only when a DM or MD says so.\r\nGET /drawers/pool reports the pool size, free drawers, and how many minted 
pieces have no drawer - plus\r\nshortfall , what a DM would have to add right now to clear the list.\r\nPOST 
/drawers/pool adds N permanent barcoded drawers and immediately drains the waiting list into them -\r\ngrowing the 
pool while leaving pieces waiting would leave a DM staring at empty drawers beside a waiting list. It is\r\ncapped at 
1000 per call as a typo guard: add: 20000 would mint twenty thousand permanent drawers and there is 
no\r\nun-mint.\r\nPOST /drawers/allocate-waiting merges drawer-less pieces into whatever drawers are currently free. 
Safe to call\r\nrepeatedly; a no-op when there is nothing to place.\r\n14. Attendance\r\nModule: 
app/modules/attendance/ · URL prefix: /api/v1/attendance\r\n14.1 Every write comes from an operator\r\nOnly four roles 
may write attendance: SECURITY, HR, MD, DM.\r\nNobody else on the floor has a login, so there is nothing else it could 
be. Both doors share one dependency, so the\r\nbarcode door and the manual door can never drift apart.\r\n14.2 Two 
doors\r\nThe barcode door (primary): POST /attendance/scan-check-in with the card code and a direction of \"in\" 
or\r\n\"out\" . The operator standing at the gate scans every card - monthly or daily, including their 
colleagues'.\r\nThe manual door (fallback): POST /attendance/proxy/check-in and /proxy/check-out when a card fails or 
is\r\nforgotten. Takes a list of employee ids. Any wage type.\r\n/attendance/check-in and /check-out are now an 
operator recording their own arrival and departure - their login\r\nis linked to an employee row. The body is 
optional; identity comes from the token and the timestamp is set server-side to\r\nblock client-side clock 
manipulation.\r\n14.3 One row per person per day\r\nwork_date uniqueness is enforced at the database level, so a 
duplicate check-in is physically impossible rather than\r\nmerely discouraged. Check-in is idempotent - a re-tap is a 
no-op.\r\nrecorded_by_user_id names the operator on every proxy entry. Accountability, and a fraud trail.\r\nThree 
flags are computed at write time so dashboards never recompute on read: is_late , is_short , is_overtime .\r\n14.4 
Shift policy is data, not code\r\nA single shift_config row holds the start time, shift length, grace minutes and the 
factory timezone - so HR can\r\nchange them without a redeploy. The timezone is the single source of truth for 
interpreting wall-clock policy and for\r\ndeciding which calendar day a punch belongs to. Storage stays UTC; the 
timezone is applied only at the business-logic\r\nand display boundaries.\r\n14.5 Location tracking is removed\r\nNo 
route asks for, validates or stores a position. Check-in succeeds on identity alone.\r\nlat and lon are still accepted 
and ignored on the bodies that used to require them, so a client that still sends\r\ncoordinates gets a 201 rather 
than a 422. The geofence columns remain mapped on the model because they are NOT\r\nNULL in Postgres with no server 
default - removing them for real is a migration, not a comment-out.\r\n14.6 It gates production\r\nProduction logging 
requires the employee to be present today. That is the link between the two modules: work\r\ncannot be recorded for 
someone who is not in the building.\r\n15. Wages\r\nModule: app/modules/wages/ · URL prefix: /api/v1/wages\r\n15.1 
Rates are date-effective\r\nA rate is (style, operation, rate, effective_from) . A mid-period rate change prices each 
day at the rate in force\r\nthat day. Nothing is retroactively re-priced.\r\nThe rate screens never show or accept a 
UUID - style_code and operation_code go in, and the service resolves\r\nthem.\r\nGET /wages/styles carries 
rated_operations / total_operations per style, so unpriced styles are visible before\r\npayroll runs and silently pays 
zero for them.\r\n15.2 Two payrolls, not one\r\nThis is the central idea of the module. The fork is on the employee 
population, and it exists because the two populations\r\nare priced by incompatible facts.\r\nrun_kind Pays Scope 
Why\r\npiece PIECE_RATE\r\nworkers\r\nstyle_code or\r\norder_number REQUIRED\r\nA piece wage is earned on a specific 
garment, so the style is the run,\r\nnot a filter on it\r\nmonthly MONTHLY\r\nsalaried staff\r\nNone required A salary 
is a fact about a person for a period. There is no honest way\r\nto say what share of a fitter's month belongs to 
CLERMONT rather\r\nthan CARNABY\r\ncombined Both - Legacy only. Never created any more\r\nThe scope requirement on a 
piece run is the guardrail. Dates alone used to be accepted, and that is how a manager\r\npays the whole factory's 
piece work under a window they meant to narrow. It is enforced at the schema (so it appears in\r\nthe OpenAPI contract 
and the frontend can grey out the button before the round trip) and repeated in the service -\r\nbecause a rule only 
the HTTP layer knows is a rule that vanishes the moment anything else calls compute.\r\nA monthly run may carry an 
order or style as a label for the payroll screen (\"the month we ran CLERMONT\"). The response\r\nechoes 
scope_is_label: true to say it did not narrow anything. The screen must not print \"CLERMONT payroll\"\r\nover a sheet 
that paid every salaried person in the building.\r\nA piece run and a monthly run over the same window do not 
conflict. Their populations are disjoint, and together\r\nthey are one complete payroll for that fortnight - compute 
both.\r\n15.3 One line per employee per run\r\nPIECE_RATE and MONTHLY are mutually exclusive - never both on one line. 
pieces is always 0 for monthly.\r\nBehind each summary line sits a wage_line_detail row per (employee, style, 
operation) cell, carrying the pieces,\r\nthe rate applied and the amount. That is what makes the three breakdown folds 
possible.\r\n15.4 The run lifecycle\r\n┌──── recompute (free) ────┐\r\n │\r\ncompute ──? OPEN ──────── close ───────? 
CLOSED\r\n │\r\n└────── reopen (+reason) ────┘\r\nDELETE ── permitted on OPEN; on CLOSED only with 
confirm_closed\r\nStatus Meaning\r\nOPEN A draft. Lines exist and can be recomputed freely - nothing has been paid 
against them, so rewriting them costs nothing\r\nCLOSED Frozen. The document the cash was counted against. Never 
silently recomputed\r\nRecompute discards the lines and rebuilds them from current production events and rates, for 
the same window and the\r\nsame scope. The run keeps its id; recompute_count increments and the actor is stamped - so 
a payslip reprinted\r\nafterwards is identifiably a different document from the one paid against.\r\nReopen is the 
only door out of CLOSED, requires a reason, and is DM/MD only. It is deliberately a separate call from\r\nrecompute: a 
manager who must press reopen, type why, then press recompute cannot rewrite a paid payslip by\r\nmistyping a run id. 
The reason is stored and belongs on every reissued payslip for that period.\r\nconfirm_closed: true on recompute is a 
one-call escape hatch. It works, it stamps the recompute, and it records no\r\nreason - which is exactly why the 
reopen door exists.\r\nClose is idempotent (a double-click changed nothing) and refuses to freeze a run with no lines 
- locking a window in\r\nwhich nobody is paid is never what was meant.\r\nDelete exists because the overlap guard has 
always named it. create_run commits an OPEN run before any line is\r\nwritten, so a compute that died halfway left a 
committed empty run permanently occupying that window, blocking every\r\nlater run over those dates, with no way to 
clear it. It refuses a CLOSED run unless explicitly confirmed: deleting a frozen\r\nrun destroys the record of a 
payment that actually happened. To change a frozen run, reopen and recompute - that\r\nkeeps the audit trail. Deleting 
is for runs that should never have existed.\r\n15.5 The overlap guard\r\nTwo runs that would pay the same money twice 
is a 409 naming the run that blocks you and what to do about it.\r\nBefore paying anyone, check two fields on the 
response:\r\nunrated_operations - stages with no rate in force. They pay zero, silently, unless you look.\r\ngap_days 
- days in the window that no run covers.\r\n15.6 The result screens\r\nEndpoint What it gives\r\n/runs/{id}/breakdown 
One frozen run folded three ways: per style (stages and workers nested), per stage factory-wide, and 
per\r\nemployee\r\n/runs/{id}/pieces Per-piece detail - which garment, which stage, which worker, their employee 
barcode, and what that\r\none piece paid\r\n/ledger Every computed run, latest computed first, searchable\r\nAll three 
breakdown folds come off the same frozen row set, so the three tabs cannot disagree with each other or with\r\nthe run 
total - which they will if the frontend sums them itself.\r\nPer-piece amounts come from the run's frozen rate for 
that cell. Nothing is re-priced, so a rate corrected after the run\r\nclosed does not change what this says the run 
paid. A row with amount: null carries a note explaining why (a monthly\r\nworker, or the stage was unrated at run 
time) - deliberately not a zero, which would read as work worth nothing.\r\nThe ledger is ordered by when a run was 
computed, not by its period: the question the ledger answers is \"what did we\r\njust run\".\r\n15.7 Who may see 
it\r\nWages are visible only to HR, DM and MD.\r\nEvery other read endpoint in this codebase uses bare 
get_current_user . These do not, because CLIENT is a real role\r\nwith a real login, and per-piece labour rates are 
the factory's cost structure. A client who can see that cutting pays\r\n12.50/pc on their own style is holding your 
margin during the next price negotiation.\r\nHR reads payroll. DM and MD authorise changes to it - recompute, reopen, 
close and delete are all DM/MD.\r\n16. Analytics and the manager dashboards\r\nModules: app/modules/analytics/ and 
app/modules/dashboard/ · Prefixes: /api/v1/analytics ,\r\n/api/v1/dashboard\r\nBoth are read-only and own no tables. 
Every query reads other modules' models.\r\n16.1 What moved, and why\r\nThe standalone Analytics Overview and Risk 
Alerts screens have been removed - they return 410 Gone with a\r\nmessage naming the replacement.\r\nThe reasoning: 
the bottleneck and the alerts were the only parts of those pages anyone acted on, and a manager should\r\nnot have to 
know a separate screen exists to find out their line is blocked. They moved onto the surface every\r\nmanager already 
opens - GET /dashboard/alerts - readable by every manager role rather than the DM alone.\r\nThey are 410 rather than 
deleted for the same reason the old production routes are: a 404 on a screen that worked\r\nyesterday reads as \"the 
server is broken\".\r\n16.2 Analytics - the drill-down\r\n/explorer ──? /orders/{id}/tree ──? /styles/{id}/detail ──? 
/pieces/detail\r\nPlus two features that stand on their own:\r\nThe piece life story ( /pieces/{code}/story ) - every 
stage a piece passed, who worked it, when, the rework flag,\r\nleather consumption at cutting, its current stage and 
what it is waiting on.\r\nConsumption vs stock ( /consumption ) - leather consumed per style, summed from cut 
events.\r\nAnalytics is a live view. Payroll of record stays the frozen wage run, and the two legitimately differ 
mid-period.\r\n16.3 The five dashboards\r\nEach is a composite - one call returns a whole screen.\r\nDashboard For 
Contains\r\nCutting Cutting\r\nManager\r\nKPIs, current order, per-cutter performance, leather lots, per-order 
progress, 14-day trend\r\nLining Lining\r\nManager\r\nThe same shape for the lining leg, plus upcoming work - 
leather-cut pieces not yet lining-cut\r\nStitching Stitching\r\nManager\r\nTop KPIs, the pre-store (fusing/pasting) 
and post-store (line/shell/final) blocks, the store handoff,\r\nthe running style's funnel, per-stage employee 
performance\r\nStore Store\r\nManager\r\nDrawer KPIs, current styles in store, the filterable drawer grid, held 
drawers, empty drawers available\r\nfor reuse\r\nDirect\r\nManager\r\nDM / MD The factory-wide control panel - 
composed from the four stage dashboards' own aggregates,\r\nso this screen and the four can never disagree\r\n16.4 The

app/modules/imports/router.py · Roles for every endpoint: DM · MD\r\n11.1 POST /imports/preview\r\nDry-run an 
breakdown workbook. Writes nothing.\r\nRequest: multipart/form-data - field order_number (form) and field file (the 
.xlsx )\r\nThe order number is validated first: a number that matches no client order is a 404, and the file is never 
parsed.\r\nResponse 200\r\n{\r\n\"clients\": 1,\r\n\"orders\": 1,\r\n\"styles\": 2,\r\n\"skus\": 5,\r\n\"pieces\": 
100,\r\n\"warnings\": [\r\n\"row 14: size '50 ' had trailing whitespace - normalised\",\r\n\"row 22: colour code 
missing, used colour name 'COGNAC'\",\r\n\"style CARNABY: no thickness in the sheet\"\r\n],\r\n\"styles_detail\": 
[\r\n{ \"name\": \"CLERMONT\", \"article\": \"A-4471\", \"skus\": 3, \"qty\": 60 },\r\n{ \"name\": \"CARNABY\", 
\"article\": \"A-4482\", \"skus\": 2, \"qty\": 40 }\r\n]\r\n}\r\nErrors\r\nCode When\r\n400 Not .xlsx / .xlsm , or not 
a valid zip container (an .xlsx is a zip; anything renamed is rejected before it reaches the\r\nparser)\r\n404 Order 
number not found\r\n413 Over max_upload_mb - streamed, aborts mid-upload\r\n11.2 POST /imports/commit\r\nParse and 
write SKUs into the named order. Idempotent.\r\nRequest: identical to 11.1.\r\nResponse 200\r\n{\r\n\"summary\": 
{\r\n\"clients\": 1, \"orders\": 1, \"styles\": 2, \"skus\": 5, \"pieces\": 100,\r\n\"warnings\": 
[]\r\n},\r\n\"written\": {\r\n\"styles_created\": 2,\r\n\"styles_updated\": 0,\r\n\"skus_created\":

\"BOG-SS27-001\",\r\n\"breakdown_url\": \"/api/v1/imports/breakdown/BOG-SS27-001\"\r\n}\r\n}\r\npieces_minted: 0 and 
release_required: true are the whole point. Commit writes DRAFT styles and SKUs.\r\nNo pieces, no barcodes, no drawer 
merges. Nothing is irreversible yet.\r\nNext call: GET /imports/breakdown/{order_number} .\r\nThe order number in this 
response is a receipt, not the only copy. The order is a permanent row, and every order is\r\nlisted at GET 
/imports/orders . Losing this response loses nothing.\r\n11.3 GET /imports/orders\r\nThe order index - the screen the

null,\r\n\"nylon_color\": null,\r\n\"style\": {\r\n\"article\": \"A-4471-B\",\r\n\"thickness\":

and both move in ONE transaction. Two round trips meant a 200 on\r\nthe SKU and a 409 on the style left the screen 
half-saved with no way to tell which half.\r\nNested style accepts: name · article · code · gender · label · thickness 
· season · customer_ref ·\r\ninternal_ref · unit_price · currency · needs_lining\r\nResponse 200 - the updated style 
block with its SKUs.\r\nErrors\r\nCode When\r\n409 The style is RELEASED. \"To make MORE of a released style, raise 
the quantity on a new upload and release again - release\r\ntops up\"\r\n409 Style code collision\r\n404 
/\r\n422\r\n11.6 PATCH /imports/breakdown/styles/{style_id}\r\nThe style-only door - for the style header, which has 
no SKU to hang off. Same body as the nested style object\r\nabove, same DRAFT-only rule, same audit row.\r\n11.7

/imports/breakdown/{order_number}/release\r\n? THE MINT\r\nThis is the single most consequential call in the system. 
It creates Piece rows, per-piece barcodes and drawer merges,\r\natomically. It cannot be undone.\r\nThree request 
shapes\r\nA - the contract. Each style carries its own answer:\r\n{\r\n\"styles\": [\r\n{ \"style_id\": 
\"4b5c6d7e-8f90-0112-2334-4556677889900\", \"needs_lining\": true },\r\n{ \"style_id\": 
\"7e8f9001-1223-3445-5667-788990011223\", \"needs_lining\": false }\r\n],\r\n\"grow_drawer_pool\": true\r\n}\r\nB - 
broadcast. One human answer covering the list. Still a declaration.\r\n{\r\n\"style_ids\": [\"4b5c6d7e-.\", 
\"7e8f9001-.\"],\r\n\"needs_lining\": true\r\n}\r\nC - deprecated. style_ids without a top-level answer falls back to 
inferring the lining requirement from the style\r\nname. Every style released this way comes back with 
lining_declared: false , and the message names them.\r\nField Type Notes\r\nstyles[] array {style_id, needs_lining} - 
preferred\r\nstyle_ids[] array Deprecated alone; fine with a top-level answer\r\nneeds_lining bool? Broadcast. A 
per-style answer overrides it\r\ngrow_drawer_pool bool Default false . Mints the drawer shortfall in the same 
call\r\nResponse 201\r\n \r\n{\r\n\"order_number\": \"BOG-SS27-001\",\r\n\"released\": [\r\n{\r\n\"style_id\": 
\"4b5c6d7e-8f90-0112-2334-4556677889900\",\r\n\"name\": \"CLERMONT\",\r\n\"needs_lining\": 
true,\r\n\"lining_declared\": true,\r\n\"pieces_minted\": 60,\r\n\"barcodes_minted\": 60,\r\n\"drawers_merged\": 
60,\r\n\"released_at\": \"2026-09-09T11:04:22.118000+00:00\",\r\n\"released_by\": \"Tanveer 
Ahmed\"\r\n}\r\n],\r\n\"rejected\": [\r\n{\r\n\"style_id\": \"7e8f9001-1223-3445-5667-788990011223\",\r\n\"name\": 
\"CARNABY\",\r\n\"reason\": \"already RELEASED on 2026-09-09T09:02:44Z - release tops up quantity 
only\"\r\n}\r\n],\r\n\"minted\": {\r\n\"pieces\": 60,\r\n\"barcodes\": 60,\r\n\"drawers_merged\": 
57,\r\n\"pieces_waiting_for_drawer\": 3\r\n},\r\n\"drawer_pool\": { \"size\": 200, \"free\": 0, \"shortfall\": 3 
},\r\n\"message\": \"Released 1 style, 60 pieces minted. 3 pieces have no drawer - grow the pool or wait for one 
to\r\n}\r\nErrors\r\nCode When\r\n422 A style with no lining answer. The message names every unanswered style and 
explains that the answer cannot be changed\r\nafter release\r\n422 styles and style_ids both sent - two lists with no 
defined precedence\r\n422 Neither sent\r\n422 Any unknown field - the body uses extra=\"forbid\" , so a misplaced 
needs_lining is named rather than silently\r\ndropped\r\n404 Order number unknown\r\nFrontend rules\r\n1. Never 
default the lining radio. null is a real state and the server rejects it.\r\n2. Read minted , not the HTTP status. 
Partial accept: an already-released style lands in rejected ; the rest still release.\r\n3. Surface 
pieces_waiting_for_drawer prominently. Those pieces have barcodes but nowhere to be stored - they\r\ncannot pass the 
merge gate.\r\n4. Warn that release is irreversible before the click.\r\nTHE SPINE\r\n12. Barcode\r\nRouter:

/attendance/me\r\nThe caller's own history. Roles: any authenticated.\r\nQuery: start · end - defaults to the last 30 
days.\r\nReturns [] when the login has no linked employee_id .\r\n18.8 GET /attendance/me/status\r\nServer-anchored 
data for a live shift countdown.\r\nResponse 200\r\n{\r\n\"employee_id\": \"c3d4e5f6-.\",\r\n\"checked_in\":

\"2026-09-09T08:14:33.221000+00:00\",\r\n\"is_late\": false,\r\n\"timezone\": \"Asia/Kolkata\"\r\n}\r\nCompute a 
one-time server_now - device_now offset and tick toward shift_end_at . Never trust the device\r\nclock.\r\n18.9 GET 
/attendance/config · PATCH /attendance/config\r\nRead: any authenticated. Write: DM · HR · MD.\r\nResponse 
200\r\n{\r\n\"shift_start\": \"09:00\",\r\n\"shift_length_hours\": 8.0,\r\n\"late_grace_minutes\": 
15,\r\n\"timezone\": \"Asia/Kolkata\"\r\n}\r\nPATCH accepts any subset. Shift policy is a database row, not config - 
HR changes it without a redeploy.\r\nThe geofence fields ( factory_lat , factory_lon , radius_m ) still exist on the 
model but are unused. The\r\nprivileged/public response split is retained in case the fence returns.\r\nMONEY\r\n19. 
Wages\r\nRouter: app/modules/wages/router.py · Roles: DM · MD · HR for reads; DM · MD only for recompute, reopen, 
close\r\nand delete.\r\nWages are not behind bare get_current_user anywhere. CLIENT is a real role with a real login, 
and per-piece\r\nlabour rates are the factory's cost structure.\r\nRoute order is load-bearing - every static segment 
is declared before /runs/{run_id} .\r\n19.1 GET /wages/orders\r\nThe payroll landing screen. Query: on (coverage date, 
default today) · unpriced_only\r\nResponse 200\r\n[\r\n{\r\n\"order_number\": \"BOG-SS27-001\",\r\n\"client_name\": 
\"BOGGI MILANO\",\r\n\"styles\": 2,\r\n\"styles_priced\": 1,\r\n\"delivery_deadline\": 
\"2026-11-30\"\r\n}\r\n]\r\nstyles_priced / styles is the card's badge. Click through to /wages/styles?order_number=. 
.\r\n19.2 GET /wages/styles\r\nQuery: order_number · client_id · unpriced_only · on\r\nResponse 
200\r\n[\r\n{\r\n\"style_code\": \"BOG-CLERMONT\",\r\n\"style_name\": \"CLERMONT\",\r\n\"order_number\": 
\"BOG-SS27-001\",\r\n\"client_name\": \"BOGGI MILANO\",\r\n\"rated_operations\": 6,\r\n\"total_operations\": 
9,\r\n\"qty_ordered\": 60\r\n}\r\n]\r\nrated_operations / total_operations is why this endpoint exists. Unpriced 
styles pay zero, silently, unless\r\nsomeone looks.\r\nStyle codes, never style ids.\r\n19.3 GET 
/wages/rate-sheet\r\nQuery: style_code (required) · on (default today)\r\nResponse 200\r\n{\r\n\"style_code\": 
\"BOG-CLERMONT\",\r\n\"style_name\": \"CLERMONT\",\r\n\"on\": \"2026-09-09\",\r\n\"rows\": [\r\n{ \"operation_code\":

/wages/rate-history\r\nQuery: style_code · operation_code (both required)\r\nResponse 200\r\n{\r\n\"style_code\":
